# Contributing to MIPStarRE

This document codifies the conventions for pull requests, issues, code review,
Lean style, and CI automation used in the MIPStarRE project.

---

## 1. Pull Request Conventions

### Title format

Use **conventional-commit** style:

```
type(scope): short description
```

| Type       | When to use                                      |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |
| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |
| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |
| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |
| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |
| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |
| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |

**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`, `blueprint`,
`LDT/Pasting`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.

Examples:
- `feat(LDT/SelfImprovement): add self-improvement induction step`
- `fix(blueprint): resolve broken labels in chapter 7`
- `refactor(LDT): extract shared preliminaries into Basic module`

### Body template

Every PR body must contain three sections. For mathematical changes, the body
should be readable by someone who has not seen the associated conversation:
cite the paper or blueprint location, give the theorem label when one exists,
and state the mathematical assertion precisely.

```markdown
### Motivation
- Why this mathematical or documentation change is needed.
- Cite the issue and, when applicable, the paper/blueprint file, line, and label.

### Description
- State precisely what changed: definitions introduced, lemmas/theorems proved,
  blueprint labels updated, and any deliberate difference from the paper statement.

### Testing
- What was verified and how.
- Examples: `lake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic.lean`, `lake build MIPStarRE`,
  `rg -n "sorry|axiom" MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic.lean || true`.

---
Addresses #N
```

Use `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge)
in the footer to link the relevant issue.

### PR template

A PR template (`.github/pull_request_template.md`) auto-fills the
Motivation / Description / Testing sections. Fill in the placeholders — do not
delete the headings.

### Local hooks

The repository includes opt-in Git hooks for catching fast statement-integrity
and blueprint-sync failures before they reach CI:

```bash
scripts/install_git_hooks.sh
scripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check
```

The pre-commit hook runs whitespace, the `scripts/tests` unit tests when any
`scripts/**/*.py` or `scripts/tests/**` file is staged, the blueprint LaTeX
convention lint (`check_blueprint_latex.py`) when blueprint sources or the
lint helper are staged, and the
paper-gap-note structure and proof-debt audits on relevant staged files,
including agent prompts and actions under `.github/`.  The pre-push hook
checks changed Lean files with `lake env lean`, repeats the fast
statement-integrity audits for relevant policy or prompt surfaces, and checks
blueprint declaration synchronization when Lean or blueprint surfaces changed.
These hooks also reject explicit `axiom` and `constant` declarations in the LDT
tree; use a tracked `sorry` for an unfinished source-faithful proof instead of
turning the missing proof into a new ambient assumption.
For larger PRs, `MIPSTARRE_HOOK_FULL=1 git push` also runs the full local gate.
Use `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` only for a one-off local-tooling bypass (the
workflow-layer line budget of `.githooks/pre-commit` still runs), and still
report the corresponding validation in the PR body.

### Labels

Apply all relevant labels from the taxonomy in [Section 4](#4-label-taxonomy).

---

## 2. Issue Conventions

### Issue templates

Three issue templates are available in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`:

| Template | When to use |
|----------|-------------|
| **Formalization Issue** | A specific theorem, definition, construction, or lemma to formalize |
| **Bug Report** | Broken proof, type error, sorry regression, statement mismatch, or CI failure |
| **Tracking Issue** | Umbrella issue for a chapter, theorem family, or proof stage, using GitHub sub-issues |

### Formalization issues

Use a descriptive, **bracket-free** title that names the mathematical content:

```
Chapter 9 — finish the sandwich-chain corollaries in ComparisonLemmas
```

Avoid prefixes like `[Chapter 9] ...`: bot-generated branch names inherit those
characters, and `]` breaks part of the PR automation stack. See
[`pr_review_management.md`](pr_review_management.md) for the rationale.

For formalization issues, usually start with `formalization` + `2009.12982`,
then add the most specific live chapter or theorem-family labels that apply (for
example `ldt-basic`, `preliminaries`, `commutativity`, `pasting`,
`main-induction`, `proof`, `proof-infra`, `statement-fix`,
`sorry-elimination`, `mismatch`, `follow-up`, `blueprint`, or
`blueprint-sync`). Documentation-only or tooling issues should use
`documentation`, `ci`, `cleanup`, and/or `refactor` instead of
`formalization`.

When the work concerns content that exists only in the blueprint and not in
the original paper (arXiv:2009.12982), apply the `blueprint-only` label
alongside the chapter or theorem-family labels.  Omit `blueprint-only` when the
work concerns a statement or definition that appears in the paper.  An issue
may need both `2009.12982` and `blueprint-only` when it spans paper-present
content and blueprint-exclusive scaffolding or auxiliary lemmas; in that case
apply both labels so the scope is explicit.

Every formalization issue must give enough mathematical source information to
make the issue self-contained:

- Paper source: a path under `references/ldt-paper/`, line number, theorem or
  equation label when available, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.
- Blueprint source: a path under `blueprint/src/chapter/`, line number, label,
  and the matching `\lean{...}` status when relevant.
- Lean target: the expected declaration name and file path, if already known.
- Dependencies: theorem labels, existing Lean declarations, and GitHub
  sub-issues that must precede the statement.

For issues or PRs touching a source-labelled theorem, include a statement
integrity check.  List the paper assumptions, the Lean assumptions, the paper
conclusion, the Lean conclusion, and a verdict: exact, faithful boundary
hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.
Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is
strongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a
documented mathematical necessity.
Faithful boundary hypotheses include formal domain data such as nonemptiness,
decidability, field-model instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator
nonvanishing when these are implicit in the source.  Extra bridge, residual,
repair, or obligation-structure assumptions are not boundary hypotheses; they
make the Lean result conditional.  Do not attach them to a paper-facing theorem.
If they are unavoidable while preserving downstream proof work, quarantine them
in a separately named conditional helper, cite the paper-gap note or tracking
issue, name the obligation discharger that must remove them, and keep the source
theorem statement visible even if its proof contains a tracked `sorry`.
For the terminology used here, see the proof-gap protocol in
[paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex).

Do not describe a mathematical issue only as a "cleanup", "follow-up", "blocked
item", or "Phase N" problem. State the theorem, lemma, definition, or mismatch
in mathematical terms first; repository labels and scheduling details come
afterward.

### Multi-part work

For a chapter or theorem family spanning several PRs, use a title pattern that
names the mathematical region and create an umbrella **tracking issue**:

```
Chapter 7 1/5: Self-improvement hypotheses
Chapter 7 2/5: Self-improvement conclusion
...
```

Attach tracked issues as **GitHub sub-issues** of the umbrella issue so GitHub
shows native progress, relationship navigation, and "Tracked by #N" links. The
issue body can keep a short human-readable index, but markdown checkboxes and
retired fenced tasklist blocks do not create native sub-issue relationships:

```markdown
### Sub-issues to attach
- #101
- #102
- #103
```

Use the issue sidebar's **Add sub-issue** control, or the REST endpoint
`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issues`, to create the
actual relationship. Put descriptions in the sub-issue titles or in prose above
the index.

### Tracking issues

Use the **Tracking Issue** template (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/tracking-issue.yml`).
Label with `tracking`; add `chapter-tracking` for the long-lived chapter
overview trackers. A tracking issue should begin by naming the mathematical
objective and citing the paper or blueprint labels that the child issues cover.
The `issue-automation` workflow will automatically:

- Rely on GitHub's native sub-issue progress instead of editing body checkboxes.
- Post progress comments on linked issues when PRs merge.
- Suggest or create `follow-up` issues for genuine deferred work called out by merged PRs.

The repository does not currently use a live `all-resolved` label, so do not
add one manually.

### Pinned issues

The three most active tracking issues are pinned to the top of the Issues tab.
Update pins when priorities shift (`gh issue pin/unpin`). GitHub allows at most
3 pinned issues.

### Milestones

Use milestones to group issues targeting a shared deadline (e.g., a paper
submission or a toolchain bump). Assign a milestone when the issue has a concrete
target date; remove it when the date no longer applies.

### Discussions

GitHub Discussions is enabled for design questions, proof strategy debates, and
topics that don't map to a single actionable issue. Use issues for concrete work
items; use discussions for open-ended conversations.

### Blueprint sync issues

When the LaTeX blueprint is out of sync with Lean code, open an issue with
the `blueprint-sync` label. Describe which chapter, theorem, or definition
needs `\lean{}` / `\leanok` tags.

Automated drift detection: the [blueprint ↔ Lean sync check][ci-sync] runs
on every PR and fails when a `\leanok` tag sits on a Lean declaration whose
transitive axiom closure still depends on `sorryAx`. See
[`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`][ci-sync] for what it checks and how to run it
locally.

[ci-sync]: ci-blueprint-sync.md

### Stale-issue audits

Issues that cite specific `sorry` sites, file/line locations, or declaration
names drift out of date as `main` moves. Keep those citations precise rather
than replacing them with vague prose: update paths, line numbers, theorem labels,
and short source paraphrases when the source moves. Before starting a new
proof-closing round (or periodically as maintenance), run the audit script to
list open issues whose citations no longer resolve:

```bash
gh issue list --repo LionSR/MIPStarRE --state open --limit 500 \
  --json number,title,body,url,labels > /tmp/open-issues.json
python3 scripts/audit_stale_issues.py --issues /tmp/open-issues.json
```

The tool is report-only. Human review decides which flags warrant closing
the issue, updating its body, or dismissing as a false positive. A weekly
read-only GitHub Actions wrapper runs the same export-and-audit sequence and
uploads an artifact only when citations are flagged. See
[`docs/stale_issue_audit.md`](stale_issue_audit.md) for the full workflow.

---

## 3. Commit Messages

- Use **imperative mood** in the subject line ("Add", not "Added").
- Keep the subject under 72 characters.
- When squash-merging a PR, the commit message should match the PR title format.
- Reference issue numbers where applicable (`(#N)` suffix or `Addresses #N` in body).

---

## 4. Label Taxonomy

This section mirrors the labels that currently exist in the GitHub repository.
If this file and `gh label list` diverge, treat GitHub as the source of truth
and update this guide in the same PR. Most formalization issues combine
`formalization` + `2009.12982` with one or more chapter or theorem-family labels.
Documentation- or tooling-only issues usually skip the paper label. Do **not**
apply legacy labels such as `self-improvement`, `expansion-graph`,

     2	#
     3	# review.sh — model-backed review of a GitHub PR, chained after a green CI.
     4	#
     5	# Usage:
     6	#   local/bin/review.sh <pr-number> [--force-review] [--dry-run]
     7	#
     8	#   <pr-number>      GitHub PR number ("12").  Branch, base and head SHA come
     9	#                    from gh_common.py pr-view; the local branch tip must be
    10	#                    exactly the GitHub head before anything is reviewed.
    11	#   --force-review   Review even when the head commit is a bot fix commit.
    12	#                    Used by autofix.sh for the single forced review at the
    13	#                    iteration cap (local/protocols/autofix.md).
    14	#   --dry-run        Resolve the worktree, diff and prompts, print where they
    15	#                    landed, and stop before dispatching an agent.
    16	#
    17	# Local replacement for .github/workflows/pr-review.yml (gate + code-review +
    18	# prose-review jobs).  Protocol: local/protocols/review.md.
    19	#
    20	# GitHub is the record (gh_common.py:4-8).  The gate reads the local-ci/summary
    21	# commit status on the exact head SHA; the verdict is published as ONE COMMENT
    22	# review bound to that SHA plus a local-review/summary status.  Single-account
    23	# repos cannot self-APPROVE, so adverseness travels in the status, never in a
    24	# review state.  There is no local PR record: a GitHub failure fails this
    25	# script closed rather than leaving a fallback record behind.
    26	#
    27	# Exit codes:
    28	#   0  review published, or an intentional skip (kill switch, bot commit, stale
    29	#      head, empty diff)
    30	#   1  usage or environment error
    31	#   3  gate blocked: local-ci/summary is not success for the head SHA.  Nothing
    32	#      is published — the absence of a green local-review/summary is the block.
    33	#   4  the reviewer returned no machine-parseable verdict trailer.  A failing
    34	#      local-review/summary is posted so the PR never reads as green.
    35	#
    36	# Environment:
    37	#   LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED       disables the reviewer on the literal string
    38	#                              "false" only; unset means enabled.
    39	#   MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF      git ref the reviewer personas are read from
    40	#                              (default: main).  Never the branch under review.
    41	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL     codex model for the code review
    42	#                              (default: gpt-5.6-sol)
    43	#   MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL      codex model for the blueprint prose review
    44	#                              (default: MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL)
    45	#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT        runtime state root (default ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev)
    46	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_LOCK_WAIT seconds to queue behind another review of the
    47	#                              same PR before giving up (default 1800)
    48	#   MIPSTARRE_DIFF_MAX_LINES   diff lines handed to the reviewer (default 4000)
    49	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT   reviewer safety timeout in seconds (default 10800)
    50	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_EFFORT    pinned reasoning effort (default ultra)

   142	sanitize_to() {
   143	  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" <<'PY'
   144	import sys
   145	src, dest, max_lines = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
   146	try:
   147	    raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   148	except OSError:

   152	for ch in raw:

   155	        keep.append(ch)
   156	lines = "".join(keep).split("\n")

   158	if len(lines) > max_lines:
   159	    truncated = len(lines) - max_lines
   160	    lines = lines[:max_lines]
   161	out = []
   162	for line in lines:
   163	    line = line.replace("```", "'''").replace("~~~", "'''")
   164	    if line.startswith("<<<") or line.startswith("# Task"):
   165	        line = " " + line

   168	    out.append("... [%d further lines omitted by review.sh; full text on disk]"

   174	# acquire_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
   175	# Per-PR review lock.  No cancellation: a queued review waits and then
   176	# re-checks the head SHA (pr-review.yml:18-20, cancel-in-progress false).
   177	acquire_lock() {
   178	  local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 holder=""
   179	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
   180	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   181	    holder="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   182	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then

   184	      rm -rf "$dir"
   185	      continue
   186	    fi
   187	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then

   219	# resolve_worktree <branch> — same resolution order as ci.sh: git's own
   220	# registry first, then the .worktrees/<branch> convention.  Creates it if the
   221	# branch has no worktree yet.
   222	resolve_worktree() {
   223	  local branch="$1" found="" safe dest have
   224	  found="$(git -C "$ROOT" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
   225	    awk -v b="refs/heads/$branch" '
   226	      /^worktree /{p=substr($0,10)}
   227	      $0 == "branch " b {print p; exit}')"
   228	  if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
   229	    printf '%s\n' "$found"
   230	    return 0
   231	  fi
   232	  safe="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
   233	  dest="$ROOT/.worktrees/$safe"
   234	  if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
   235	    have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
   236	    if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
   237	      printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   238	      return 0
   239	    fi
   240	    die "$dest exists but is not a worktree of '$branch' (HEAD: ${have:-not a git worktree}); run 'git -C $ROOT worktree prune' or remove it"
   241	  fi
   242	  mkdir -p "$ROOT/.worktrees"
   243	  git -C "$ROOT" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" ||
   244	    die "git worktree add $dest $branch failed"
   245	  if [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" ]; then
   246	    "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" "$dest" >&2 ||
   247	      warn "worktree-setup.sh failed for $dest; the reviewer runs without a warmed build cache"
   248	  else
   249	    warn "local/bin/worktree-setup.sh not found; the reviewer worktree has no warmed Lean build cache (local/protocols/build-cache.md)"
   250	  fi
   251	  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   252	}

   254	# run_agent <role> <sandbox> <worktree> <persona-path> <task-file>
   255	#           <standalone-prompt> <context-file> <out-file> <model>
   256	#
   257	# All codex invocations go through local/bin/dispatch.sh when it exists, so the
   258	# session lands in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl (DESIGN.md, "Agent
   259	# sessions").  The fallback is a direct codex exec with a loud warning.

   261	  local role="$1" sandbox="$2" wt="$3" persona="$4" taskfile="$5"
   262	  local standalone="$6" ctx="$7" out="$8" model="$9"
   263	  local dlog="$out.dispatch.log" task_text last rc=0
   264	  task_text="$(cat "$taskfile")"
   265	
   266	  if [ -x "$DISPATCH" ]; then
   267	    local args
   268	    args=(--role "$role" --issue "pr$PR_NUM" --pr "$PR_NUM"
   269	          --worktree "$wt" --sandbox "$sandbox"
   270	          --persona "$persona" --persona-ref "$TRUSTED_REF"
   271	          --effort "$REVIEW_EFFORT")
   272	    if [ -n "$ctx" ]; then
   273	      args[${#args[@]}]="--context-file"
   274	      args[${#args[@]}]="$ctx"
   275	    fi
   276	    if [ -s "$RUN_DIR/prior-ledger.md" ]; then
   277	      args[${#args[@]}]="--context-file"
   278	      args[${#args[@]}]="$RUN_DIR/prior-ledger.md"
   279	    fi
   280	    args[${#args[@]}]="--"
   281	    args[${#args[@]}]="$task_text"
   282	    # One retry for pre-model failures: a dispatch that dies within seconds
   283	    # with zero tokens never reached the model (transient CLI/API hiccup;
   284	    # observed on PR #0003, events.md 2026-08-31), so retrying cannot
   285	    # duplicate a review.
   286	    local attempt started ended tokens
   287	    for attempt in 1 2; do
   288	      started="$(date +%s)"
   289	      set +e
   290	      if [ -n "$model" ]; then
   291	        MIPSTARRE_SESSION_TIMEOUT="$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 \
   292	          MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL="$model" "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   293	      else
   294	        MIPSTARRE_SESSION_TIMEOUT="$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 \
   295	          "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   296	      fi
   297	      rc=$?
   298	      set -e
   299	      ended="$(date +%s)"
   300	      tokens="$(sed -n 's/^tokens_total: //p' "$dlog" | tail -1)"
   301	      if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && [ "$attempt" -eq 1 ] \
   302	         && [ "$(( ended - started ))" -lt 15 ] \
   303	         && [ "${tokens:-0}" = "0" ]; then
   304	        warn "dispatch failed pre-model (rc=$rc, $(( ended - started ))s, 0 tokens); retrying once"
   305	        sleep 10
   306	        continue
   307	      fi
   308	      break
   309	    done
   310	    last="$(sed -n 's/^last_message: //p' "$dlog" | tail -1)"
   311	    if [ -n "$last" ] && [ -f "$last" ]; then
   312	      cp "$last" "$out"
   313	    fi
   314	    if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
   315	      warn "dispatch.sh exited $rc; its output is at $dlog"
   316	    fi
   317	    return "$rc"
   318	  fi
   319	
   320	  warn "local/bin/dispatch.sh not found; falling back to a direct 'codex exec'. This session will NOT appear in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl."
   321	  command -v codex >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
   322	    die "codex CLI not found on PATH and no local/bin/dispatch.sh to delegate to"
   323	  set +e
   324	  if [ -n "$model" ]; then
   325	    MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 timeout --signal=TERM "$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" codex exec --sandbox "$sandbox" -C "$wt" </dev/null \
   326	      -m "$model" -o "$out" -- "$(cat "$standalone")" >"$dlog"
   327	  else
   328	    MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 timeout --signal=TERM "$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" codex exec --sandbox "$sandbox" -C "$wt" </dev/null \
   329	      -o "$out" -- "$(cat "$standalone")" >"$dlog"
   330	  fi
   331	  rc=$?
   332	  set -e
   333	  return "$rc"
   334	}

   698	# -------------------------------------------------------- review file writer
   699	# write_review <kind> <agent-out> <dest> <session-label> <model>

   701	write_review() {
   702	  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" \
   703	    "$PR_NUM" "$BRANCH" "$BASE" "$MERGE_BASE" "$HEAD_SHA" "$4" "$(now_utc)" "$5" "$REVIEW_EFFORT" <<'PY'
   704	import os, re, sys
   705	
   706	(kind, agent_out, dest, pr, branch, base, merge_base, head_sha,
   707	 session, generated, model, effort) = sys.argv[1:13]
   708	
   709	try:
   710	    body = open(agent_out, encoding="utf-8").read()
   711	except OSError:
   712	    sys.stderr.write("review.sh: the reviewer produced no output file\n")
   713	    raise SystemExit(2)

   715	body = body.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").strip("\n")
   716	
   717	# --- verdict trailer (mandatory) -----------------------------------------
   718	verdict = None
   719	for line in reversed([l.strip() for l in body.split("\n") if l.strip()][-8:]):
   720	    m = re.fullmatch(r"VERDICT:\s*(APPROVED|COMMENTED|CHANGES_REQUESTED)", line)

   722	        verdict = m.group(1)

   727	        "the reviewer's last message (%s)\n" % agent_out)

   738	        continue

   745	# verdict trailer are re-emitted by this writer in fixed positions.

   755	    r"^\s*[-*]\s*\[( |x|X|-)\]\s*F?\d*\s*\(([^)]*)\)\s*`([^`]*)`\s*[—–-]+\s*(.*)$")

   763	        continue

   768	            sev = "advisory" if ("advis" in sev or "nit" in sev) else "changes"

   775	if not entries and verdict != "APPROVED":

   777	        "changes", "-",
   778	        "reviewer returned %s without a machine-readable findings list; read the "
   779	        "review body and resolve this by hand" % verdict))

   781	ledger = ["- [ ] F%d (%s) `%s` — %s" % (n, sev, loc, summary)

   787	# not the record: what pr_merge.py reads is the published COMMENT review whose
   788	# body combine_review builds out of these two files.

   793	       "pr: %s" % pr,
   794	       "kind: %s" % kind,
   795	       "branch: %s" % branch,
   796	       "base: %s" % base,
   797	       "merge_base: %s" % merge_base,

   806	       "",
   807	       "# %s review — PR %s @ %s" % (kind.capitalize(), pr, head_sha[:12]),
   808	       "",
   809	       "Local replacement for the `%s` job of `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`." % job,
   810	       "",
   811	       "## Findings",
   812	       "",
   813	       "Checkbox states: `[ ]` unresolved (blocks the merge), `[x]` resolved,",
   814	       "`[-]` outdated (the cited lines were rewritten; does not block).",
   815	       "",
   816	       "<!-- findings:begin -->"]

   851	  python3 - "$COMBINED_MD" "$CODE_MD" "$PROSE_MD" "$1" "$2" "$3" \

   868	    for line in text.split("\n"):
   869	        stripped = line.strip()
   870	        if stripped == "<!-- findings:begin -->":
   871	            keep = True
   872	            continue
   873	        if stripped == "<!-- findings:end -->":
   874	            keep = False
   875	            continue

   877	            findings.append(line.rstrip())

   898	       "VERDICT: %s (code=%s, prose=%s)" % (worst, code_verdict or "none",
   899	                                            prose_verdict or "n/a"),
   900	       "",
   901	       "Posted by `local/bin/review.sh` at %s — the local replacement for the "
   902	       "`code-review` and `prose-review` jobs of `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`."

   907	       "## Findings",
   908	       "",
   909	       "Checkbox states: `[ ]` unresolved (blocks the merge), `[x]` resolved.",

   912	       "<!-- findings:begin -->"]

   915	if prose_verdict:

   917	out.append("")

   920	                           prefix=".combined-", suffix=".tmp")

GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
status signal; the REST `line` field lied.

Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:

    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis

| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
|---|---|---|
| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |

`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.

**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.

Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
next review re-derives from the new diff.

A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`

`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;
`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR
proliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on
branch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name
validation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming
(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).

The local translation is:

| Parent | Local | Who starts it |
|---|---|---|
| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
| auto-fix workflows | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode ...` | CI/review chain or a human |

`agent.sh` is **never invoked by automation.**  `claude.yml:24-30` gated the
responder on `sender.type != 'Bot'` because a bot echoing `@claude` into a
comment would start a write-enabled, secret-bearing session; the local form is
that `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` export `MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1` (and
`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1`) around every agent they run, and `agent.sh`
refuses to start when either is set.  `agent.sh` also refuses while a fix lock
is held for its branch: two writers on one branch is the parallel-push
collision that `auto-fix.yml:253-256` serialised away.

The author_association gate has no local analogue and is dropped — the human
running the command *is* the authorisation.  The `]`-in-branch-name lesson
survives as a lint in all three scripts.

`agent.sh` may commit; it must not use the `[codex-auto-fix]` /
`[codex-review-fix]` prefixes, because a human-directed commit must be
reviewable and those prefixes make the reviewer skip.  The script warns if the
session used one anyway.

The auto-create-PR step of `claude.yml` becomes a printed instruction rather
than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).

## 11. Operating it

    local/bin/review.sh 7                # review PR 0007 at its current head
    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch

Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
neither publishes a review.

Artefacts:

| Path | Committed | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |

Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so
the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
agreeing is intentional redundancy.

Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
not a verdict.

## 12. Deliberately not ported

Untouched-code or new-mechanism findings are "out of scope -> issue #N".

* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
  One reviewer session; the cascade
  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS > CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER > anthropic` becomes
  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
  comes from a branch of this single repository.
* **Thread resolution via `mcp__github__resolve_review_thread`.**  Replaced by
  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.
* **`allowed-tools` presets and `allowed-tools.json`.**  codex sandbox modes
  (`read-only` for review, `workspace-write` for fixes) carry the same intent
  with a coarser grain: read-only genuinely prevents writes, which the
  allow-list only approximated.
* **`id-token`/OAuth plumbing, `LionSR/agent-ci-actions`, plugin marketplaces.**
  Local codex configuration replaces them (`.codex/`, `local/protocols/sessions.md`).


## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)

A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:

1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   `moot: <reason>`);
2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.

Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.
# Protocol: issues and pull requests

Normative for the GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle and the automation in
`local/bin/`; read `local/protocols/meta.md` first. The repository is
`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`, and GitHub is the **single source of truth** for
issues, PRs, CI and review evidence, and merges; CI and reviews still *execute*
here and publish their results there. No active `issues/` or `prs/` tree, no
shadow record, no write-through cache, no offline mutation mode: a GitHub error
fails the operation, never a local success (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01).

## 1. Records, names, tools

Issues and PRs are GitHub's, identified by their numbers — no zero-padded ids,
no frontmatter. Parent/child structure is the native sub-issue relation
(`POST …/issues/{parent}/sub_issues`), one parent per issue exactly as the
retired `parent:` scalar allowed; discussion is comments; labels come from the
repository (`list-labels`, paginated), so `local/labels.yml` is retired and a
label absent from GitHub is reported, never invented. Briefs (the design record
per issue) live in `local/briefs/`: agent input, not lifecycle state.

Every GitHub call goes through `local/bin/gh_common.py` — a module for Python
callers, and for the shell scripts a CLI (`pr-view`, `post-status`,
`latest-statuses`, `ensure-pr-comment`, `post-review`, `merge-pr`,
`issue-create`, `issue-close`, `snapshot`, …; `--help` lists them) owning CLI
discovery, repository resolution, API version headers, bounded retry of
transient failures and the exit-2-with-stderr convention. Nothing else shells
out to `gh`. `issue_new.py`, `issue_close.py`, `pr_open.py`, `ci.sh`,
`review.sh`, `autofix.sh`, `pr_merge.py`, `github-sync.sh` take GitHub numbers;
`track.py`, `validate_tree.py` and `export_issues.py` are deleted.

* Branches: `issue-<github-number>-<slug>`, or `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>`
  from an agent; `pr_open.py` rejects what `git check-ref-format` would.
* Titles, slugs and branch names are **bracket-free**: bot-generated branch
  names inherit those characters and "`]` breaks part of the PR automation
  stack" (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124). A `:` in a *title* is fine
  (`Tracking: …`), but not in a branch.
* `autofix.sh`'s automated fix commits keep the exact subject prefixes
  `[codex-auto-fix]` and `[codex-review-fix]`; its iteration counter and the
  review skip key on them.  Operator and worker repairs use plain
  `fix(review): …` / `fix(ci): …` subjects so the reviewer sees them.
* `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` auto-closes the issue on merge, `Addresses #N` does
  not (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:61-62) — and the numbers being GitHub's, that
  footer is now literally what GitHub itself reads.

## 2. Evidence contracts

All evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).

**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one
`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,
`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,
`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.
`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`
after it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads
the *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined
status, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one
PR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by
`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.

**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,
carrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the
line `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.
Unchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`; clean means
`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`
too — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review
event carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`
(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.

**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with
`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition
line per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.

**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated
read finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating
it (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than
webhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.

## 3. The merge gate

`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,
never push `main`. The merge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact
`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge
commit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates
that refuse by default:

1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely
   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;
2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip
   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here;
3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on
   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state
   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;
4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or
   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is
   `success` there;
5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;
6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder);
   the count of `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts with a §1 fix
   prefix is printed for the record and is not a gate;
7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not
   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.

`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when
an exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.

Afterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the
remote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local
dirt defers it with a warning).

## 4. Untrusted text

Issue and PR bodies are untrusted data, and **more** so now that they arrive
from GitHub: anyone with repository access, and every imported external report,
writes the fields that are echoed into generated markdown and interpolated into
agent prompts. All three parent workflows sanitized before interpolation, and
`wf_util.sanitize` is that step ported: strip control characters, break fenced
code with zero-width spaces, truncate to 200 characters for titles and 5000 for
bodies (issue-automation.yml:122-128).

Every LLM hook in `local/bin` carries the same four requirements: gate on
`MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED != "false"`; read prompts from committed main
(`git show main:…`), never the branch under review (DESIGN.md:76-77); frame
sanitized text as data that must not be followed; and filter any model-proposed
label through the repository's label list. `audit_stale_issues.py` additionally
keeps its path-traversal rejection for externally sourced citations.

## 5. Environment, snapshot, archive

`MIPSTARRE_GH` is the path to `gh` (else `PATH`, else the documented user-local
location); `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` overrides the `owner/name` otherwise read
from the `github` remote; `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` (default 5) bounds `autofix.sh`'s
own loop only — the merge gate does not read it — and is operator-tunable with
the reason recorded in `results/telemetry/events.md`, unlike
`MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE` (the pre-commit budget), the one owner-gated control
in the layer. `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` and
`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` keep kill-switch semantics (DESIGN.md:73-75).

`github-sync.sh` pushes explicit refs and writes an atomic, paginated read-only
snapshot of open issues and PRs to `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/`
(`open-issues.json`, `open-pulls.json`, `metadata.json`; PRs filtered out of the
issue endpoint) — audit and recovery telemetry, never lifecycle input. The
retired trees stay archived under `results/telemetry/registry-archive/` (commit
c8f1999): read-only research data, never edited or read as active input.

   139	# sanitize_to <src> <dest> <max-lines> — control-char strip, fence breaking,
   140	# truncation (DESIGN.md invariant 6).  dispatch.sh sanitizes attachments again;
   141	# this is the copy that also protects the no-dispatcher fallback path.
   142	sanitize_to() {
   143	  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" <<'PY'
   144	import sys
   145	src, dest, max_lines = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
   146	try:
   147	    raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   148	except OSError:
   149	    raw = ""
   150	raw = raw.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
   151	keep = []
   152	for ch in raw:
   153	    o = ord(ch)
   154	    if ch in "\n\t" or (32 <= o < 127) or o > 159:
   155	        keep.append(ch)
   156	lines = "".join(keep).split("\n")
   157	truncated = 0
   158	if len(lines) > max_lines:
   159	    truncated = len(lines) - max_lines
   160	    lines = lines[:max_lines]
   161	out = []
   162	for line in lines:
   163	    line = line.replace("```", "'''").replace("~~~", "'''")
   164	    if line.startswith("<<<") or line.startswith("# Task"):
   165	        line = " " + line
   166	    out.append(line)
   167	if truncated:
   168	    out.append("... [%d further lines omitted by review.sh; full text on disk]"
   169	               % truncated)
   170	open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out) + "\n")
   171	PY
   172	}

   174	# acquire_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
   175	# Per-PR review lock.  No cancellation: a queued review waits and then
   176	# re-checks the head SHA (pr-review.yml:18-20, cancel-in-progress false).
   177	acquire_lock() {
   178	  local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 holder=""
   179	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
   180	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   181	    holder="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   182	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
   183	      warn "removing stale lock $dir (holder pid $holder is gone)"
   184	      rm -rf "$dir"
   185	      continue
   186	    fi
   187	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   188	      die "timed out after ${wait_s}s waiting for the review lock $dir (holder pid ${holder:-unknown})"
   189	    fi
   190	    [ "$waited" = 0 ] && log "another review holds $dir (pid ${holder:-unknown}); queuing"
   191	    sleep 5
   192	    waited=$((waited + 5))
   193	  done
   194	  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   195	  printf '%s\n' "$label" >"$dir/label"
   196	  LOCK_HELD="$dir"
   197	}

   219	# resolve_worktree <branch> — same resolution order as ci.sh: git's own
   220	# registry first, then the .worktrees/<branch> convention.  Creates it if the
   221	# branch has no worktree yet.
   222	resolve_worktree() {
   223	  local branch="$1" found="" safe dest have
   224	  found="$(git -C "$ROOT" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
   225	    awk -v b="refs/heads/$branch" '
   226	      /^worktree /{p=substr($0,10)}
   227	      $0 == "branch " b {print p; exit}')"
   228	  if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
   229	    printf '%s\n' "$found"
   230	    return 0
   231	  fi
   232	  safe="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
   233	  dest="$ROOT/.worktrees/$safe"
   234	  if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
   235	    have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
   236	    if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
   237	      printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   238	      return 0
   239	    fi
   240	    die "$dest exists but is not a worktree of '$branch' (HEAD: ${have:-not a git worktree}); run 'git -C $ROOT worktree prune' or remove it"

241	  fi
   242	  mkdir -p "$ROOT/.worktrees"
   243	  git -C "$ROOT" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" ||
   244	    die "git worktree add $dest $branch failed"
   245	  if [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" ]; then
   246	    "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" "$dest" >&2 ||
   247	      warn "worktree-setup.sh failed for $dest; the reviewer runs without a warmed build cache"

   249	    warn "local/bin/worktree-setup.sh not found; the reviewer worktree has no warmed Lean build cache (local/protocols/build-cache.md)"
   250	  fi
   251	  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   252	}

   254	# run_agent <role> <sandbox> <worktree> <persona-path> <task-file>

   256	#
   257	# All codex invocations go through local/bin/dispatch.sh when it exists, so the

   279	    fi
   280	    args[${#args[@]}]="--"
   281	    args[${#args[@]}]="$task_text"
   282	    # One retry for pre-model failures: a dispatch that dies within seconds
   283	    # with zero tokens never reached the model (transient CLI/API hiccup;
   284	    # observed on PR #0003, events.md 2026-08-31), so retrying cannot
   285	    # duplicate a review.
   286	    local attempt started ended tokens
   287	    for attempt in 1 2; do
   288	      started="$(date +%s)"
   289	      set +e
   290	      if [ -n "$model" ]; then
   291	        MIPSTARRE_SESSION_TIMEOUT="$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 \
   292	          MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL="$model" "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   293	      else
   294	        MIPSTARRE_SESSION_TIMEOUT="$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 \
   295	          "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   296	      fi
   297	      rc=$?
   298	      set -e
   299	      ended="$(date +%s)"
   300	      tokens="$(sed -n 's/^tokens_total: //p' "$dlog" | tail -1)"

   302	         && [ "$(( ended - started ))" -lt 15 ] \

   304	        warn "dispatch failed pre-model (rc=$rc, $(( ended - started ))s, 0 tokens); retrying once"

   306	        continue
   307	      fi
   308	      break
   309	    done
   310	    last="$(sed -n 's/^last_message: //p' "$dlog" | tail -1)"

   312	      cp "$last" "$out"
   313	    fi
   314	    if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
   315	      warn "dispatch.sh exited $rc; its output is at $dlog"
   316	    fi
   317	    return "$rc"
   318	  fi
   319	
   320	  warn "local/bin/dispatch.sh not found; falling back to a direct 'codex exec'. This session will NOT appear in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl."
   321	  command -v codex >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
   322	    die "codex CLI not found on PATH and no local/bin/dispatch.sh to delegate to"
   323	  set +e
   324	  if [ -n "$model" ]; then
   325	    MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 timeout --signal=TERM "$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" codex exec --sandbox "$sandbox" -C "$wt" </dev/null \
   326	      -m "$model" -o "$out" -- "$(cat "$standalone")" >"$dlog"
   327	  else
   328	    MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 timeout --signal=TERM "$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" codex exec --sandbox "$sandbox" -C "$wt" </dev/null \
   329	      -o "$out" -- "$(cat "$standalone")" >"$dlog"
   330	  fi
   331	  rc=$?
   332	  set -e
   333	  return "$rc"
   334	}

   859	NUMBER = re.compile(r"^(\s*[-*]\s*\[[ xX-]\]\s*)F\d+(\s*)")

   872	            continue

   874	            keep = False
   875	            continue

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	#
     3	# review.sh — model-backed review of a GitHub PR, chained after a green CI.
     4	#
     5	# Usage:
     6	#   local/bin/review.sh <pr-number> [--force-review] [--dry-run]
     7	#
     8	#   <pr-number>      GitHub PR number ("12").  Branch, base and head SHA come
     9	#                    from gh_common.py pr-view; the local branch tip must be
    10	#                    exactly the GitHub head before anything is reviewed.
    11	#   --force-review   Review even when the head commit is a bot fix commit.
    12	#                    Used by autofix.sh for the single forced review at the
    13	#                    iteration cap (local/protocols/autofix.md).
    14	#   --dry-run        Resolve the worktree, diff and prompts, print where they
    15	#                    landed, and stop before dispatching an agent.
    16	#
    17	# Local replacement for .github/workflows/pr-review.yml (gate + code-review +
    18	# prose-review jobs).  Protocol: local/protocols/review.md.
    19	#
    20	# GitHub is the record (gh_common.py:4-8).  The gate reads the local-ci/summary
    21	# commit status on the exact head SHA; the verdict is published as ONE COMMENT
    22	# review bound to that SHA plus a local-review/summary status.  Single-account
    23	# repos cannot self-APPROVE, so adverseness travels in the status, never in a
    24	# review state.  There is no local PR record: a GitHub failure fails this
    25	# script closed rather than leaving a fallback record behind.
    26	#
    27	# Exit codes:
    28	#   0  review published, or an intentional skip (kill switch, bot commit, stale
    29	#      head, empty diff)
    30	#   1  usage or environment error
    31	#   3  gate blocked: local-ci/summary is not success for the head SHA.  Nothing
    32	#      is published — the absence of a green local-review/summary is the block.
    33	#   4  the reviewer returned no machine-parseable verdict trailer.  A failing
    34	#      local-review/summary is posted so the PR never reads as green.
    35	#
    36	# Environment:
    37	#   LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED       disables the reviewer on the literal string
    38	#                              "false" only; unset means enabled.
    39	#   MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF      git ref the reviewer personas are read from
    40	#                              (default: main).  Never the branch under review.
    41	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL     codex model for the code review (default: the
    42	#                              dispatcher's / codex's own default)
    43	#   MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL      codex model for the blueprint prose review
    44	#                              (default: MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL)
    45	#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT        runtime state root (default ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev)
    46	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_LOCK_WAIT seconds to queue behind another review of the
    47	#                              same PR before giving up (default 1800)
    48	#   MIPSTARRE_DIFF_MAX_LINES   diff lines handed to the reviewer (default 4000)
    49	#   MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO      owner/repo override for gh_common.py

   105	# json_get <file> <dotted-path> — one scalar out of a gh_common JSON payload.
   106	# Absent keys print an empty line, so callers test with [ -n ... ] as they did
   107	# with the frontmatter reader this replaces.
   108	json_get() {
   109	  python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
   110	import json, sys
   111	try:
   112	    data = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
   113	except Exception as exc:
   114	    sys.stderr.write("review.sh: unreadable GitHub payload %s: %s\n" % (sys.argv[1], exc))
   115	    raise SystemExit(1)
   116	for part in sys.argv[2].split("."):
   117	    data = data.get(part) if isinstance(data, dict) else None
   118	print("" if data is None else data)
   119	PY
   120	}

   131	# sanitize_to <src> <dest> <max-lines> — control-char strip, fence breaking,
   132	# truncation (DESIGN.md invariant 6).  dispatch.sh sanitizes attachments again;
   133	# this is the copy that also protects the no-dispatcher fallback path.
   134	sanitize_to() {
   135	  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" <<'PY'
   136	import sys
   137	src, dest, max_lines = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
   138	try:
   139	    raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   140	except OSError:
   141	    raw = ""
   142	raw = raw.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
   143	keep = []
   144	for ch in raw:
   145	    o = ord(ch)
   146	    if ch in "\n\t" or (32 <= o < 127) or o > 159:
   147	        keep.append(ch)
   148	lines = "".join(keep).split("\n")
   149	truncated = 0
   150	if len(lines) > max_lines:
   151	    truncated = len(lines) - max_lines
   152	    lines = lines[:max_lines]
   153	out = []
   154	for line in lines:
   155	    line = line.replace("```", "'''").replace("~~~", "'''")
   156	    if line.startswith("<<<") or line.startswith("# Task"):
   157	        line = " " + line
   158	    out.append(line)
   159	if truncated:
   160	    out.append("... [%d further lines omitted by review.sh; full text on disk]"
   161	               % truncated)
   162	open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out) + "\n")
   163	PY
   164	}

   166	# acquire_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
   167	# Per-PR review lock.  No cancellation: a queued review waits and then
   168	# re-checks the head SHA (pr-review.yml:18-20, cancel-in-progress false).
   169	acquire_lock() {
   170	  local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 holder=""
   171	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
   172	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   173	    holder="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   174	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
   175	      warn "removing stale lock $dir (holder pid $holder is gone)"
   176	      rm -rf "$dir"
   177	      continue
   178	    fi
   179	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   180	      die "timed out after ${wait_s}s waiting for the review lock $dir (holder pid ${holder:-unknown})"
   181	    fi
   182	    [ "$waited" = 0 ] && log "another review holds $dir (pid ${holder:-unknown}); queuing"
   183	    sleep 5
   184	    waited=$((waited + 5))
   185	  done
   186	  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   187	  printf '%s\n' "$label" >"$dir/label"
   188	  LOCK_HELD="$dir"
   189	}

   203	# committed default branch, never from the branch under review (DESIGN.md
   204	# invariant 5; pr-review.yml:140-146, the .trusted-actions checkout).
   205	fetch_trusted() {
   206	  if ! git -C "$ROOT" show "$TRUSTED_REF:$1" >"$2" 2>/dev/null; then
   207	    die "cannot read trusted prompt '$1' from ref '$TRUSTED_REF'. The reviewer persona must come from committed $TRUSTED_REF (DESIGN.md invariant 5); commit .github/prompts/ there or set MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF."

   211	# resolve_worktree <branch> — same resolution order as ci.sh: git's own
   212	# registry first, then the .worktrees/<branch> convention.  Creates it if the
   213	# branch has no worktree yet.
   214	resolve_worktree() {
   215	  local branch="$1" found="" safe dest have
   216	  found="$(git -C "$ROOT" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
   217	    awk -v b="refs/heads/$branch" '
   218	      /^worktree /{p=substr($0,10)}
   219	      $0 == "branch " b {print p; exit}')"
   220	  if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
   221	    printf '%s\n' "$found"
   222	    return 0
   223	  fi
   224	  safe="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
   225	  dest="$ROOT/.worktrees/$safe"
   226	  if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
   227	    have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
   228	    if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
   229	      printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   230	      return 0
   231	    fi
   232	    die "$dest exists but is not a worktree of '$branch' (HEAD: ${have:-not a git worktree}); run 'git -C $ROOT worktree prune' or remove it"
   233	  fi
   234	  mkdir -p "$ROOT/.worktrees"
   235	  git -C "$ROOT" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" ||
   236	    die "git worktree add $dest $branch failed"
   237	  if [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" ]; then
   238	    "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" "$dest" >&2 ||
   239	      warn "worktree-setup.sh failed for $dest; the reviewer runs without a warmed build cache"
   240	  else
   241	    warn "local/bin/worktree-setup.sh not found; the reviewer worktree has no warmed Lean build cache (local/protocols/build-cache.md)"
   242	  fi
   243	  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   244	}

   246	# run_agent <role> <sandbox> <worktree> <persona-path> <task-file>
   247	#           <standalone-prompt> <context-file> <out-file> <model>
   248	#
   249	# All codex invocations go through local/bin/dispatch.sh when it exists, so the
   250	# session lands in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl (DESIGN.md, "Agent
   251	# sessions").  The fallback is a direct codex exec with a loud warning.
   252	run_agent() {
   253	  local role="$1" sandbox="$2" wt="$3" persona="$4" taskfile="$5"
   254	  local standalone="$6" ctx="$7" out="$8" model="$9"
   255	  local dlog="$out.dispatch.log" task_text last rc=0
   256	  task_text="$(cat "$taskfile")"
   257	
   258	  if [ -x "$DISPATCH" ]; then
   259	    local args
   260	    args=(--role "$role" --issue "pr$PR_NUM" --pr "$PR_NUM"
   261	          --worktree "$wt" --sandbox "$sandbox"
   262	          --persona "$persona" --persona-ref "$TRUSTED_REF")
   263	    if [ -n "$ctx" ]; then
   264	      args[${#args[@]}]="--context-file"
   265	      args[${#args[@]}]="$ctx"
   266	    fi
   267	    args[${#args[@]}]="--"
   268	    args[${#args[@]}]="$task_text"
   269	    # One retry for pre-model failures: a dispatch that dies within seconds
   270	    # with zero tokens never reached the model (transient CLI/API hiccup;
   271	    # observed on PR #0003, events.md 2026-08-31), so retrying cannot
   272	    # duplicate a review.
   273	    local attempt started ended tokens
   274	    for attempt in 1 2; do
   275	      started="$(date +%s)"
   276	      set +e
   277	      if [ -n "$model" ]; then
   278	        MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL="$model" \
   279	          "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   280	      else
   281	        MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   282	      fi
   283	      rc=$?
   284	      set -e
   285	      ended="$(date +%s)"
   286	      tokens="$(sed -n 's/^tokens_total: //p' "$dlog" | tail -1)"
   287	      if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && [ "$attempt" -eq 1 ] \
   288	         && [ "$(( ended - started ))" -lt 15 ] \
   289	         && [ "${tokens:-0}" = "0" ]; then
   290	        warn "dispatch failed pre-model (rc=$rc, $(( ended - started ))s, 0 tokens); retrying once"
   291	        sleep 10
   292	        continue
   293	      fi
   294	      break
   295	    done
   296	    last="$(sed -n 's/^last_message: //p' "$dlog" | tail -1)"
   297	    if [ -n "$last" ] && [ -f "$last" ]; then
   298	      cp "$last" "$out"
   299	    fi
   300	    if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
   301	      warn "dispatch.sh exited $rc; its output is at $dlog"
   302	    fi
   303	    return "$rc"
   304	  fi
   305	
   306	  warn "local/bin/dispatch.sh not found; falling back to a direct 'codex exec'. This session will NOT appear in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl."
   307	  command -v codex >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
   308	    die "codex CLI not found on PATH and no local/bin/dispatch.sh to delegate to"
   309	  set +e
   310	  if [ -n "$model" ]; then
   311	    MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 codex exec --sandbox "$sandbox" -C "$wt" \
   312	      -m "$model" -o "$out" -- "$(cat "$standalone")" >"$dlog"
   313	  else
   314	    MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 codex exec --sandbox "$sandbox" -C "$wt" \
   315	      -o "$out" -- "$(cat "$standalone")" >"$dlog"
   316	  fi
   317	  rc=$?
   318	  set -e
   319	  return "$rc"
   320	}

   324	FORCE_REVIEW=0

   354	# GitHub is the record: branch, base and head SHA come from the PR itself, so
   355	# there is no local metadata to drift out of date (gh_common.py:4-6).
   356	case "$PR_ARG" in
   357	  ""|*[!0-9]*) die "'$PR_ARG' is not a GitHub PR number; usage: $PROG <pr-number> [--force-review] [--dry-run]" ;;

   361	RUN_ROOT="$CACHE/reviews/pr$PR_NUM"

   368	BASE="$(json_get "$PR_JSON" base.ref)"
   369	HEAD_SHA="$(json_get "$PR_JSON" head.sha)"
   370	PR_STATE="$(json_get "$PR_JSON" state)"

   372	[ -n "$BRANCH" ]   || die "PR #$PR_NUM has no head branch in the GitHub payload"
   373	[ -n "$HEAD_SHA" ] || die "PR #$PR_NUM has no head SHA in the GitHub payload"

   390	# The reviewer reads the local worktree, so the local tip and the GitHub head

   392	# GitHub head that describes different local bytes is worse than no verdict.
   393	LOCAL_TIP="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$BRANCH^{commit}" || true)"

   395	  die "branch '$BRANCH' does not exist locally; check it out (or fetch it) before reviewing PR #$PR_NUM"

   400	# ------------------------------------------------------------------- CI gate
   401	# pr-review.yml:59-61 — a non-success CI conclusion FAILS the gate.  It must
   402	# never read as a green review.  The evidence is the local-ci/summary commit
   403	# status bound to this exact head SHA (local/protocols/issues-prs.md); no local
   404	# manifest is consulted, and no fallback is invented when GitHub is unreachable.
   405	gate_block() {
   406	  printf '%s: %s\n' "$PROG" "$1" >&2
   407	  printf '%s: gate blocked for PR %s @ %s; nothing published (an absent local-review/summary is the block)\n' \
   408	    "$PROG" "$PR_NUM" "$HEAD_SHA" >&2
   409	  exit 3
   410	}

   412	CI_SUMMARY="$(ghc latest-statuses "$HEAD_SHA" >"$RUN_ROOT/statuses.json" &&
   413	  json_get "$RUN_ROOT/statuses.json" 'local-ci/summary.state' || true)"
   414	case "$CI_SUMMARY" in
   415	  success) ;;
   416	  "") gate_block "no local-ci/summary status on $HEAD_SHA (or GitHub is unreachable); run local/bin/ci.sh $PR_NUM on this head SHA before reviewing" ;;
   417	  *)  gate_block "local-ci/summary is '$CI_SUMMARY' for $HEAD_SHA; review is blocked until CI is green on this head SHA" ;;
   418	esac

   420	# ------------------------------------------------------------ bot-commit gate
   421	# pr-review.yml:69-79 — skip auto-fix bot commits so the review -> fix -> review
   422	# cascade cannot start.  The exact prefixes are load-bearing (DESIGN.md
   423	# invariant 2 and the "Fix commits" naming rule).
   424	HEAD_SUBJECT="$(git -C "$ROOT" log -1 --format=%s "$HEAD_SHA")"
   425	# The subject comes from the commit under review: neutralise block markers and
   426	# control characters before it is quoted into a prompt.
   427	HEAD_SUBJECT_SAFE="$(printf '%s' "$HEAD_SUBJECT" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\037' |
   428	  sed 's/<<</< < </g; s/>>>/> > >/g' | cut -c1-160)"
   429	if printf '%s' "$HEAD_SUBJECT" | grep -qE "$BOT_PREFIX_RE"; then
   430	  if [ "$FORCE_REVIEW" -eq 0 ]; then
   431	    log "head commit is a bot fix commit ($HEAD_SUBJECT); skipping review. Pass --force-review for the terminal review at the iteration cap."
   432	    exit 0
   433	  fi
   434	  log "head commit is a bot fix commit; --force-review given, reviewing the final bot-fix result"
   435	fi

   438	LOCK_DIR="$CACHE/locks/review-$PR_NUM.lock"
   439	acquire_lock "$LOCK_DIR" "$LOCK_WAIT" "review pr=$PR_NUM sha=$HEAD_SHA"

   441	# A fix in flight rewrites the very worktree the reviewer reads.  Concurrency
   442	# keys differ on purpose (per-PR for reviews, per-branch for fixes), so this
   443	# cross-check has to be explicit.
   444	FIX_LOCK="$CACHE/locks/fix-$(printf '%s' "$BRANCH" | tr '/' '-').lock"
   445	if [ -d "$FIX_LOCK" ]; then
   446	  FIX_PID="$(cat "$FIX_LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   447	  if [ -n "$FIX_PID" ] && kill -0 "$FIX_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
   448	    log "autofix.sh (pid $FIX_PID) is rewriting $BRANCH; exiting rather than reviewing a moving tree. Re-run after CI on the new head."
   449	    exit 0
   450	  fi
   451	fi

   453	# head_moved — true when either side of the pair (local branch tip, GitHub PR
   454	# head) has left $HEAD_SHA.  Both are re-read: a fix commit can land locally, be
   455	# pushed, or both, while this review waits for the lock or for the model.
   456	head_moved() {
   457	  local tip current
   458	  tip="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$BRANCH^{commit}" || true)"
   459	  if [ -n "$tip" ] && [ "$tip" != "$HEAD_SHA" ]; then
   460	    printf 'local %s is at %s\n' "$BRANCH" "$tip"
   461	    return 0
   462	  fi
   463	  current="$(ghc pr-view "$PR_NUM" >"$RUN_ROOT/pr-view-recheck.json" &&
   464	    json_get "$RUN_ROOT/pr-view-recheck.json" head.sha || true)"
   465	  if [ -z "$current" ]; then
   466	    printf 'GitHub head of PR #%s is unreadable\n' "$PR_NUM"
   467	    return 0
   468	  fi
   469	  if [ "$current" != "$HEAD_SHA" ]; then
   470	    printf 'GitHub head of PR #%s is %s\n' "$PR_NUM" "$current"
   471	    return 0
   472	  fi
   473	  return 1
   474	}

   477	if MOVED="$(head_moved)"; then
   478	  log "head moved off $HEAD_SHA while this review was queued ($MOVED); exiting without a verdict"
   479	  exit 0
   480	fi

   532	# ------------------------------------------------------------- prompt builder
   533	# build_task <kind> <trusted-task-file> <dest> — the trusted review prompt plus

   550	# Local execution contract (authoritative where it conflicts with the above)

   552	This review runs on a local checkout of a real GitHub PR.  You are the reviewer,
   553	not the publisher: review.sh posts your verdict as the single COMMENT review for
   554	this head SHA.

   557	  comments, reviews or statuses yourself.  A second review for the same head SHA

   560	  API, put that content in your final message instead.

   564	  blueprint/src/chapter/, AGENTS.md, docs/project_conventions.md and
   565	  docs/CONTRIBUTING.md §5 (the review checklist you are applying, unchanged by
   566	  the move to GitHub-native records).
   567	
   568	PR context:
   569	  PR number        $PR_NUM
   570	  Branch           $BRANCH
   571	  Base             $BASE
   572	  Merge base       $MERGE_BASE
   573	  Head SHA         $HEAD_SHA
   574	  Head subject     $HEAD_SUBJECT_SAFE
   575	  Review kind      $kind
   576	  Worktree         $WORKTREE
   577	  Trigger          local-ci/summary is success for this head SHA
   578	
   579	# Required output format
   580	
   581	Your final message IS the review.  It must contain, in this order:
   582	
   583	1. A section headed exactly \`## Findings\`.  Every issue you would have posted
   584	   as an inline review comment becomes exactly one line, in exactly this shape:
   585	
   586	       - [ ] F1 (blocker) \`MIPStarRE/Path/File.lean:123\` — one-line summary

   597	   not write here is not tracked anywhere else.

   602	
   603	       VERDICT: APPROVED
   604	       VERDICT: COMMENTED

   614	# build_standalone <persona-file> <task-file> <ctx-file> <dest> — the whole

   633	# preserve_prior <dest> — a re-review at the same SHA replaces the ledger, and

   645	# -------------------------------------------------------- review file writer
   646	# write_review <kind> <agent-out> <dest> <session-label> <model>
   647	# prints "verdict=X" and "unresolved=N"; exits 2 with no usable verdict.
   648	write_review() {
   649	  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" \
   650	    "$PR_NUM" "$BRANCH" "$BASE" "$MERGE_BASE" "$HEAD_SHA" "$4" "$(now_utc)" "$5" <<'PY'
   651	import re, sys
   652	
   653	(kind, agent_out, dest, pr, branch, base, merge_base, head_sha,
   654	 session, generated, model) = sys.argv[1:12]
   655	
   656	try:
   657	    body = open(agent_out, encoding="utf-8").read()
   658	except OSError:
   659	    sys.stderr.write("review.sh: the reviewer produced no output file\n")
   660	    raise SystemExit(2)
   661	
   662	body = body.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").strip("\n")
   663	
   664	# --- verdict trailer (mandatory) -----------------------------------------
   665	verdict = None
   666	for line in reversed([l.strip() for l in body.split("\n") if l.strip()][-8:]):
   667	    m = re.fullmatch(r"VERDICT:\s*(APPROVED|COMMENTED|CHANGES_REQUESTED)", line)
   668	    if m:
   669	        verdict = m.group(1)
   670	        break
   671	if verdict is None:
   672	    sys.stderr.write(
   673	        "review.sh: no 'VERDICT: APPROVED|COMMENTED|CHANGES_REQUESTED' trailer in "
   674	        "the reviewer's last message (%s)\n" % agent_out)
   675	    raise SystemExit(2)
   676	
   677	# --- split off the agent's own Findings section ---------------------------
   678	lines = body.split("\n")
   679	head_re = re.compile(r"^#{1,4}\s")
   680	find_re = re.compile(r"^#{1,4}\s+Findings\s*$", re.IGNORECASE)
   681	start, end = None, len(lines)
   682	for i, line in enumerate(lines):
   683	    if find_re.match(line):
   684	        start = i
   685	        continue
   686	    if start is not None and head_re.match(line):
   687	        end = i
   688	        break
   689	raw_findings = lines[start + 1:end] if start is not None else []
   690	rest = (lines[:start] + lines[end:]) if start is not None else lines
   691	# The body keeps the reviewer's prose only: its own "## Review" heading and the
   692	# verdict trailer are re-emitted by this writer in fixed positions.
   693	rest = [l for l in rest
   694	        if not re.fullmatch(r"#{1,4}\s+Review\s*", l.rstrip())
   695	        and not re.match(r"^\s*VERDICT:\s*(APPROVED|COMMENTED|CHANGES_REQUESTED)\s*$", l)]
   696	rest = "\n".join(rest).strip("\n")
   697	
   698	# --- canonicalise the ledger ---------------------------------------------
   699	# Two shapes: with the location in backticks (what the contract asks for) and
   700	# without (what reviewers actually type when they forget).
   701	LINE_BT = re.compile(
   702	    r"^\s*[-*]\s*\[( |x|X|-)\]\s*F?\d*\s*\(([^)]*)\)\s*`([^`]*)`\s*[—–-]+\s*(.*)$")
   703	LINE_PL = re.compile(
   704	    r"^\s*[-*]\s*\[( |x|X|-)\]\s*F?\d*\s*\(([^)]*)\)\s*(\S*)\s*[—–-]+\s*(.*)$")
   705	SEVERITIES = {"blocker", "changes", "advisory"}
   706	entries = []
   707	for line in raw_findings:
   708	    text = line.strip()
   709	    if not text or text.lower().lstrip("-*[] ").rstrip() == "none":
   710	        continue

   713	        sev = m.group(2).strip().lower()
   714	        if sev not in SEVERITIES:
   715	            sev = "advisory" if ("advis" in sev or "nit" in sev) else "changes"

   717	        entries.append((sev, loc, m.group(4).strip()))
   718	    else:
   719	        # Never drop something the reviewer put in the findings section.
   720	        entries.append(("changes", "-", "unparsed finding: " + text.lstrip("-* ")))

   722	if not entries and verdict != "APPROVED":
   723	    entries.append((
   724	        "changes", "-",
   725	        "reviewer returned %s without a machine-readable findings list; read the "
   726	        "review body and resolve this by hand" % verdict))

   728	ledger = ["- [ ] F%d (%s) `%s` — %s" % (n, sev, loc, summary)
   729	          for n, (sev, loc, summary) in enumerate(entries, start=1)]

   733	# review_state carries the verdict verbatim.  The lane file is runtime state,
   734	# not the record: what pr_merge.py reads is the published COMMENT review whose
   735	# body combine_review builds out of these two files.
   736	state = verdict
   737	job = "code-review" if kind == "code" else "prose-review"
   738	
   739	out = ["---",
   740	       "pr: %s" % pr,
   741	       "kind: %s" % kind,
   742	       "branch: %s" % branch,
   743	       "base: %s" % base,
   744	       "merge_base: %s" % merge_base,
   745	       "head_sha: %s" % head_sha,
   746	       "verdict: %s" % verdict,
   747	       "review_state: %s" % state,
   748	       "session: %s" % session,
   749	       "model: %s" % (model or "(dispatcher default)"),
   750	       "generated: %s" % generated,
   751	       "---",
   752	       "",
   753	       "# %s review — PR %s @ %s" % (kind.capitalize(), pr, head_sha[:12]),
   754	       "",
   755	       "Local replacement for the `%s` job of `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`." % job,
   756	       "",
   757	       "## Findings",
   758	       "",
   759	       "Checkbox states: `[ ]` unresolved (blocks the merge), `[x]` resolved,",
   760	       "`[-]` outdated (the cited lines were rewritten; does not block).",
   761	       "",
   762	       "<!-- findings:begin -->"]
   763	out.extend(ledger)

   765	            "",
   766	            "## Review",
   767	            "",
   768	            rest,
   769	            "",
   770	            "## Verdict",
   771	            "",
   772	            "VERDICT: %s" % verdict,
   773	            ""])
   774	import os, tempfile
   775	fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=os.path.dirname(dest) or ".",
   776	                           prefix=".verdict-", suffix=".tmp")

   778	    fh.write("\n".join(out))

   781	print("verdict=%s" % verdict)
   782	print("unresolved=%d" % sum(1 for line in ledger if line.startswith("- [ ]")))
